The constructor above throws an error in case if the ptr is null out of the new string creation.
This constructor blindly accepts user's input. Any reason for this? Should not it be validated as well?
I moved the code to be common and moved the error into this constructor.  Not sure what else we want to do here.  PTAL.
Igor, I value your opinion here but I want to get this series off the stack.
If I can make edits here in the future, please let me know, but I think I've done what you've asked.
It's been working, so it's fine to keep it as it is.
Please consider using ASN1_STRING_get0_data and ASN1_STRING_length instead of direct field access: https://openssl-library.org/post/2026-04-13-asn1_string/index.html
Updated to use the helpers.
Should these be private?
Yes, they should.  Fixed and added constructor.
I don't see it's called from anywhere. Should it be removed?
Yes, it should.  Removed.
It seems this function should also be converted to RAII using the OpenSSLEVPKeyCTX wrapper.

It should be, but I don't have time this moment, so this was the best rebase I could do.  I believe this is now only used in a method you wrote recently in init below.  Is that something you could stack a patch to do?
Sure, please check Gunnar's comments, and I will work on this after you publish updated diff.

I'm open to this change, but I don't have time for it this moment.  Something you could stack a patch to do?

This looks wrong 

`name.release()) > 0` ?

```
sk_GENERAL_NAME_push() (which maps to OPENSSL_sk_push) returns the new total number of elements in the stack on success, and  or a negative value on error (usually failure to allocate memory). 
```

Prior to this we had ASSERT_EQ(sk_GENERAL_NAME_push(gens, gen), 1);

With that said, i've changed it.
